From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Johnson <evan.johnson@lyra-systems.com>, Sara Perez <sara.perez@lyra-systems.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap & next steps — Redwood Inference

Hi Evan / Sara,

Thanks again for the time today — appreciated the deep dive into Lyra's vector search and question-answering use cases. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we’re aligned: 

- Goal: reduce nearest-neighbor search latency for customer support retrieval from ~320ms to <120ms while cutting per-query GPU cost via batching/caching.
- Tech priorities: on-prem privacy boundary (VPC+KMS), SLA for 99th pct latency, and predictable throughput for batch ingest.
- Proposed Redwood approach: Dedicated pool with prefix KV caching, model quantization profile (8-bit), and a short pilot (4 weeks) to validate latency/cost on a representative workload.

Next steps I suggest:
1) I’ll send a draft mutual action plan and a 4-week pilot SOW for your review (attached).
2) If that looks good, propose a 30-min follow-up next week to finalize scope and an internal list of success metrics.
3) If you prefer, we can connect you with our solutions engineer for a quick architecture walkthrough.

Attached: mutual_action_plan.xlsx (draft).

If you’re still interested, can you confirm preferred time windows next Tue/Wed? If your priorities have shifted, a quick reply with “not a priority” is totally fine — that helps us follow up appropriately.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
